question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $V$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-\frac{1}{2},2],$ compute $P(-1\le V<\frac{1}{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $V$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(v)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le v\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $V$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-\frac{1}{2},2],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(v)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}, & -\frac{1}{2}\le v\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1\le V<\frac{1}{2}) & =P(-\frac{1}{2}\le V<\frac{1}{2}) \\  & ={\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}f(v)\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}\frac{2}{5}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}-(-\frac{1}{2})}{\frac{5}{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
